clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote to her sister daily; Walter spent long hours away from home; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees; by September, June had joined the church choir and her anxiety eased. These shifts in the household and the extended family pile up over eighteen months as the family settled into the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, within the year: Walter drank heavily; he and Glen blamed each other; Glen took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened; Nora began wetting the bed; her grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found; by October, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning trees. The shifts pile up among Walter, Glen, Carl and Nora over seventeen months as the family moved to Ridgeport and adjusted to the loss.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975, within the year and a half: Glen sat out of work in the truck for hours; he and Marian fought over money; Marian took a second job; Nora stopped eating; she kept to her room away from her mother; Walter drank again after six years; by June 1976, Nora was eating again and made the track team. The shifts pile up among Glen, Marian, Nora and Walter over sixteen months as the family weathered the cannery closure.

clusters.name: Wilma moved in, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990, within the year and a half: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's care; Sam worked late and kept his distance; Sam took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared; Nora and Sam had rows most nights; by June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts pile up among Nora, Sam, Wilma and the children over eighteen months as the household adjusted to the new arrangement.

clusters.name: Tess's drinking, 1996–1997
clusters.reason: In the fall of 1996, Tess began drinking most nights; Nora phoned her every night, worried; Tess and Rick had shouting matches and he slept at his brother's; by June 1997, Tess stopped drinking and went to meetings twice a week. Two shifts that count—Tess's symptom up and Nora's anxiety up—with Nora's worry and Marian's overfunctioning beside them over nine months, held together as one person's trouble and the family's reaction: no one else's shifts show in these months apart from the household's moves around Tess.
